chunks: Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Khālid, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
A bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Advise me, O Messenger of Allah!' He replied, 'Yes, I advise you to guard that which is between your legs.'

key_terms.حِفْظُ مَا بَيْنَ رِجْلَيْكَ: Guarding that which is between the legs (chastity/modesty)

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's advice to the bedouin regarding chastity?
ai.summary: In the context of *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq (a) emphasizes that guarding one's chastity is the foundational act of asceticism (*zuhd*), extending beyond mere legal prohibition to a spiritual discipline of self-restraint. This advice, originally directed to the Prophet (s) in some interpretations or transmitted as a universal principle, underscores the Shia scholarly view that physical modesty is the gateway to broader ethical purity and silence. The instruction reflects the holistic Islamic ethic where controlling the lower self (*nafs*) is prerequisite to mastering speech and action.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 14.Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Khālid, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said,
“A bedouin came to the Prophet (ṣ) and said, ‘Advise me, O Messenger of Allah!’ He (ṣ) replied, ‘Yes. I advise you to guard that which is between your legs.’” [1]
